clue.text: One reportedly has to decrease medication

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the word is taken for its sound

blocks.note: one person speaking of themself says I, which sounds like this organ of sight
to decrease is to fall or lower

explanation.surface: Someone is told they must cut down on their medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the answer is 'I drop', a person announcing that they decrease something.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyedrop is a liquid medicine dripped into the eye, so it is a form of medication.

clue.text: Demands and gets precise amount of old money

blocks.note: precise means exact
s is the abbreviation for a shilling, a coin of pre-decimal British currency

explanation.surface: Someone insists on, and receives, the right sum in pre-decimal coins.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's money before 1971 was pounds, shillings and pence (£sd), so s stands for a shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact something is to insist on it and obtain it, a synonym of demands as a verb.

clue.text: Team consumed by anger about liquid containing drug

indicators.note: something consumed ends up inside the eater, so the team goes inside the word for anger
about can mean turned round, as in about-face, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: to rile is to anger
a cricket or football team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A furious team is in trouble over a spiked drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The team goes inside first, and only then is the whole thing turned round; 'about' is not a second container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a sweetened liquid preparation carrying a medicine, or a magical potion.

clue.text: Circuitous part of traffic system

blocks.note: first meaning: indirect, going the long way round
second meaning: a circular junction where traffic flows round a central island

explanation.surface: A winding stretch of a road network.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for an indirect route and a noun for a circular road junction, common in Britain.

clue.text: Winnie briefly taking lithium for serious condition

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the bear's surname is dropped
taking means holding something within, so the chemical symbol goes inside

blocks.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is A. A. Milne's bear
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: A beloved bear is put on a mood-stabilising drug for a grave illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Winnie-the-Pooh is the full name of the bear, so 'Winnie' alone leads to his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Polio is a viral disease that can cause paralysis, so it is a serious medical condition.

clue.text: Twisted boy and caused an injury

blocks.note: wound is the past tense of wind, to twist
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy twisted something and hurt someone.
explanation.walkthrough: WOUND here rhymes with sound, but in the answer it is the injury word.
explanation.definitionFit: To wound someone is to injure them, so the past tense matches having caused an injury.

clue.text: Eccentric Lib Dem won southwest London constituency

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters fall out of their usual order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unconventional Liberal Democrat candidate took a London seat in a general election.
explanation.walkthrough: Lib Dem is short for Liberal Democrat, a British political party; the constituency is home to the tennis championships.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimbledon is a district and parliamentary constituency in southwest London, famous for tennis.

clue.text: Ruin a French party

blocks.note: un is French for a
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Wrecking a party held in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo can mean to bring about someone's downfall, a synonym of ruin as a verb.

clue.text: Finally informed European Commission about coal mine that is crumbling

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of informed
the usual abbreviation for the European Commission
re means about or concerning
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Brussels has finally been briefed on a colliery that is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' looks like part of the wordplay (IE) but here it only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit describes something worn out and falling into ruin through age, much like crumbling.

clue.text: SAS tried frantically to provide cover for debacle

indicators.note: acting frantically means wildly and without order, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Special forces scrambled to hush up a fiasco.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS is the Special Air Service, a British army special forces regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, humiliating failure, which is a synonym of a disaster.

clue.text: "Goodbye", said DI Rebus evenly

indicators.note: evenly suggests the even-numbered positions, so the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on are kept

blocks.note: letters two, four, six, eight and ten of these words

explanation.surface: A fictional detective takes his leave with a farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a mere link but supplies the first kept letter; Rebus is Ian Rankin's Edinburgh detective inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French borrowed into English as a farewell, a synonym of goodbye.

clue.text: Ma suckled pathetic, helpless creatures

indicators.note: pathetic means feeble or poorly made, suggesting these letters are badly put together and must be reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother nursed feeble, defenceless young animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Lame ducks are people or things that are weak and ineffective, figuratively helpless beings unable to cope.

clue.text: After an interval promise to protect 50 developing nations

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so the number sits inside the word for promise

blocks.note: in music a third is an interval of three notes
to give your word is to promise
L is 50 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: After a pause, a pledge to safeguard fifty poorer countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the order: the promise, holding L, comes after the musical interval.
explanation.definitionFit: The Third World is a dated term for the poorer, less industrialised countries, now usually called developing nations.

clue.text: Character in Greek mythology taking back Egyptian port

indicators.note: back signals going the other way, so the port's name is read from end to start

blocks.note: Suez is a port at the southern end of the Suez Canal

explanation.surface: A mythical figure reclaims a harbour on the Nile delta's side of Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus is the king of the gods in ancient Greek myth, so he is a figure in that mythology.

clue.text: I scour URLs, which could be interpreted as defamatory

indicators.note: something interpreted is given a new reading, so these letters can be read in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone combs through web addresses that might be read as libellous.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurrilous remarks are abusive and damaging to a person's reputation, close to defamatory in meaning.

clue.text: A cordial monk

blocks.note: first meaning: a herbal liqueur made in France
second meaning: a member of the order founded by St Benedict

explanation.walkthrough: 'cordial' looks like an adjective for a friendly monk, but here it is a noun, a sweet alcoholic drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The liqueur was named after the order of monks said to have first made it, so one name covers both.

clue.text: Be close to someone on Ramsay Street?

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, to be next to or adjoin
second meaning: a character in the soap opera set on that street

explanation.surface: Asking whether living near someone makes you part of a famous fictional street.
explanation.walkthrough: Ramsay Street is the setting of Neighbours, a long-running Australian TV soap hugely popular in Britain; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for lying beside something and a noun for a resident living next door.

clue.text: Quiet cry followed by a surprising noise during children's game

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
eek is a cry of alarm
taken as written
boo is said to startle someone

explanation.surface: A hushed shriek then a startling sound in the middle of a game for toddlers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' looks like a container signal but only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Peekaboo is a game played with babies, hiding the face and then revealing it.

clue.text: Late December got milder

blocks.note: Dec is the calendar abbreviation for December
weather that eased became gentler

explanation.surface: The weather turned less harsh towards the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' seems to describe December but it is the definition, in its sense of no longer living.
explanation.definitionFit: Late in 'the late king' means dead, a synonym of deceased.

clue.text: Administrator's routine is to play hangman

indicators.note: to play with something is to move it about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: an exec is an executive, an administrator; the 's reads as has
these letters reworked

explanation.surface: A manager's habit is a game of hangman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hangman' reads as the pencil-and-paper game but is the definition: someone who hangs people.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangman carries out death sentences by hanging, so he is an executioner.

clue.text: Useless series of books that's about a sailor

indicators.note: about means around, so the abbreviation for that is wraps the sailor

blocks.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a series of books of the Bible
ie, Latin id est, means that is
OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A worthless run of volumes about life at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible counts as a series of books, which is why its Old Testament is clued this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose means serving no practical purpose, a formal synonym of useless.

clue.text: Merchant has traditional sovereign

blocks.note: trad is short for traditional, as in trad jazz
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A dealer owns an old-fashioned gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is also an old British gold coin, which fits the merchant picture; here it means a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant buys and sells goods, which is what a trader does.

clue.text: Sharp cry

blocks.note: first meaning: having a fine cutting edge
second meaning: to wail in mourning, as at an Irish funeral

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a shrill shout; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means having a fine edge, and also, from Irish, to lament loudly for the dead.

clue.text: Thief who must be very strong?

definitions.text: Thief who must be very strong?

blocks.clueFragment: Thief who must be very strong?
blocks.note: surface reading: a burly criminal capable of heavy lifting
setter's reading: someone who steals from a store, imagined as hoisting the whole building

explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' is slang for steal; taken literally, a person who lifts a whole store would need great strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the usual word for someone who steals goods from a retail outlet.

clue.text: Worships Almighty without devotional words

indicators.note: here without means with the outside parts removed, leaving the run of letters at the centre

blocks.note: the run of letters across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone praises God without using prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, especially one of those in the Bible, so it is words of devotion.

clue.text: Articulate wrong tense

indicators.note: to articulate is to pronounce, so the next word is taken for its spoken sound

blocks.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Pronounce the incorrect verb form, says a grammar teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks grammatical but means tight; the homophone works in British pronunciation, where the r in the legal word is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut means pulled tight, a synonym of tense as an adjective.

clue.text: A star pursuing stud for a dance

indicators.note: something pursuing comes behind, so the first phrase is placed after the next word

blocks.note: a boss is a raised stud or knob
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A celebrity chases a ladies' man to get a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian dance and musical style related to samba.

clue.text: Very into eggs, Arachne would shortly become egg-shaped

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the abbreviation is placed within the pair of letters for eggs

blocks.note: O looks like an egg, so two eggs are OO
v is the usual abbreviation for very
Arachne is the setter, so she would is I would, contracted to I'd

explanation.surface: The setter, very keen on eggs, imagines herself turning oval.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym; here it stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid comes from the Latin for egg and describes a solid with an egg's rounded oval form.

clue.text: Part of foothold's terribly crumbly

indicators.note: part of signals that only a piece of the following words is wanted

blocks.note: the letters sit across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A section of a climbing hold is badly falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbly' looks like an adjective for rock but is British slang for an old person.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumbly is jokey British slang for an elderly person, and an oldster is an old person too.

clue.text: Erasmus dressed up in rubber

indicators.note: dressing up changes appearance, so these letters are given a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Renaissance scholar wears latex clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubber' reads as the material but is the definition: one who rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur gives massages, kneading the body, so he is literally someone who rubs.
